reviews.review: i like these tables in general, the retro tables are pretty interesting to play albeit not attention-keeping for long stretches. Rest of the tables, even the EM's are good. I really enjoy the EM+ and Remake tables. Comes with Time Machine (Solid-State) for free, it's a pretty good table. Zaccaria, looking forward to what you come up with next, cause i will keep buying. I haven't tried any of the game-licensed boards like Postal or Blood West, but I am curious and interested in these and will likely buy them shortly since i enjoyed the games themselves.

Solid pinball action. Camera controls took a while to take in - the default view shows the full table, but you can zoom in to get closer to the action for a better experience.

I was enjoying it, until the AI art slop-fest started. I was tolerant of it at first, but less so as the art has started to look not so good. The thing is, as consumers, we really have no way of knowing how much AI is being used or how it impacted the employees at a company. We only have your word for staffing levels, and corporations lie all the time, more so when it makes them money. Disclosing it isn't going to win you an award; that's literally required to be on Steam at all. So stating you're being transparent about it in your FAQ doesn't make you a great company. It just means you follow the rules.

The problem with AI art is even when you pay for it, the engines are built of art scraped from the web. Art that does not belong to the AI art generating license people. They are thieves, and even if you pay them for a license, you are still generating art using someone else's hard work and not paying them for it. In any other industry this would be called stealing. Because the laws haven't caught up with AI art yet, you can get away with it, but that doesn't make it right guys. You are profiting off of someone else's hard work and not paying them for it.

Back to Pinball FX for me. While Zen is also greedy, at least they haven't hopped on the AI bandwagon yet.

FWIW, I only made this review because you locked the post talking about AI art in the forums. If it bothers you that people are talking about what you're doing, then you probably did something wrong.

Update Sep '25: Very good, major update, executed well.

I'm a proud owner of the Platinum Edition.  As of this review I have all 82*** tables, but they are making and releasing new tables on a regular basis. Zaccaria was an actual pinball machine manufacturer in Italy from 1974-1990. At their peak they were the third largest manufacturer of pinball machines behind leaders Bally and Williams. 

Their first efforts were EM (Electro-Mechanical) tables. 12 of those have been released so far (most recently "Topical," originally manufactured in 1974). An excellent table by-the-way. This was offered as DLC just this month.  Naturally Zaccaria transitioned to Solid State tables.  There are 27 SS tables released so far. I say 'so far' because beginning in 1988 Zaccaria was reorganized and renamed Mr. Game.  While only a few Zaccaria tables remain unreleased none of the 6 Mr. Game tables have been added. By-the-way, five tables were released from 1988-90 under the Tecnoplay name. Those remain undigitized as well.

But that's not all. Zaccaria has been remaking their original tables as if they were made today, complete with DMDs. They have released 16 'Remake" tables so far. They recently added "Winter Sports 2018" as DLC, which is a complete redesign of "Winter Sports" manufactured in 1978. But that's not all, and besides they're not even at the halfway mark with their remakes yet. They also have been releasing "Retro" tables. What are they? Demakes, if that's a word. Redesigning their tables as if they came out in the 1950s or 60s. There are 18 of those so far. I haven't seen them offered as DLC yet, but as a Platinum Package owner they are added for free.** They say you need to renew the Platinum Package to get everything at a discount, but I haven't had too yet.  If you buy the Platinum Package and then later add DLC, you're only charged for what is added AFTER you bought the Platinum Package, at a prorated rate. I never recall having to pay for the Retro tables though. They just show up in my game. This month "Magic Castle Retro" and "Clown Retro" were added to my table collection.

Additionally, there are Award tables. 9 so far (10 if you count the one that I haven't unlocked yet). Just this month the best Award table was released (so far), and that's "Zombie." It was added because I had already bought the Platinum Package. Some can be earned thru Achievements. Most (well all but one) can be bought as DLC. They aren't based on any real Zaccaria tables.

There are a ton of Achievements to unlock. 12-20+ per table.  

Each table can be played with 1-4 players with 3 or 5 balls. Additionally there are 3 main modes. Arcade. Simulation. User. Some Achievements can only be unlocked in Simulation mode, plus mini-games Checkpoint, Challenge, Survivor, Lamp Hunter, Target Eliminator, and 90 Sec. Every mode, variation, and mini-game has it's own Leaderboard.

This game puts to shame "The Pinball Arcade," with a ton of adjustments, which can be made to everything you can imagine! That's not an overstatement.  Zaccaria Pinball has been in Early Access for about 2 years, but they are forever tweaking things and adding features, so it's worth it.

The physics are reasonable and the flippers responsive. In User Mode these things can be customized to your liking. In fact everything is customizable. At least I can't think of any options that Magic Pixel has missed in this area.

EDITED TO ADD THE FOLLOWING DETAILS:

There is also VR support, but I haven't reviewed that aspect of the game, because while I own the VR support DLC I don't as yet own a VR setup.

The following tables were originally Special tables for Silver and Gold members. They are included in the Platinum membership of course. They are all digitized versions of actual Zaccaria Electro-Mechanical and Solid State tables:

"Cine Star"
"Nautilus"
"Pinball Champ '83"
"Red Show"
"Supersonic"
"Universe"
"Wood's Green"

I don't recall exactly when the Platinum membership became available, but it was after I had bought the Gold membership. 

ACCORDING TO ZACCARIA:

SILVER BUNDLE:
This bundle includes original 36 table DLCs (37 tables) together at a reduced price.
If you already own some of the DLC in the bundle, the cost of this bundle will be further reduced proportionately.

GOLD BUNDLE:
This bundle includes original 36 Zaccaria table DLCs (37 tables) and Bronze Membership DLC.*
If you already own some of the DLC in the bundle, the cost of this bundle will be further reduced proportionately.

PLATINUM BUNDLE:
This bundles has ALL the Zaccaria Pinball products released and all new products will be added to this bundle the day they get released.

If you already own some of the DLC in the bundle, the cost of this bundle will be further reduced proportionately and when you own this bundle the next products you can buy with discount via this bundle.

*I don't believe they are still offering the Bronze bundle. If they are it's not listed on the Store Page for this game. I seem to remember owning it at one time.

**I need to claify this point. Once you own a digitized table, either Solid State or Electro-Mechanical, you get the Retro table of the same name for free. For example, owning the "Clown" table means that you will also get the "Clown Retro" table for free. I own every digitized Zaccaria table released to date. So, I get the Retro tables at no extra charge when released. I don't need to do anything. They just show up in my table inventory automatically.

***More tables are added monthly. I now own 95 tables.
